findings.span: After the recommended starting dose is established, all subsequent participants will receive the same fixed dose throughout the Phase 1/2 study, with no lower- or higher-dose cohorts planned.
findings.claim: This rules out the planned dose escalation and randomized comparison of two candidate doses. It also prevents evaluation of dose–response before selecting the RP2D.
findings.guidance_quote: The goal of dosage optimization is to identify the dosage(s) that maximizes the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of the drug.

findings.span: For the randomized Phase 2 portion, each of the three active-dose arms will be compared independently with placebo using an unadjusted two-sided α=0.05 test, with the study considered positive if any single dose comparison reaches nominal significance.
findings.claim: The three active-dose arms and placebo contradict the stated two-candidate-dose randomization and single-RP2D Phase 2 objective. Declaring success after any of three unadjusted tests also fails to control the overall false-positive rate.
findings.guidance_quote: Critical to quality factors are attributes of a trial that are fundamental to the protection of participants, the reliability and interpretability of the trial results, and the decisions made based on the trial results.

findings.span: Dose selection for expansion will be based solely on the dose-limiting toxicity rate observed during the first treatment cycle, without incorporating findings from other studies or analyses of the complete clinical database.
findings.claim: First-cycle DLT alone excludes later toxicity, tolerability, PK, PD, efficacy and relevant external data, contradicting the stated integrated RP2D criteria.
findings.guidance_quote: The selected dosage should be supported by a comprehensive evaluation of available data, including pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, safety, and efficacy data.

findings.span: For the new pembrolizumab–investigational-agent combination in metastatic colorectal cancer, the study will proceed directly to the expansion cohort at 200 mg every three weeks without evaluating alternative dose levels.
findings.claim: This is a different cancer population and combination regimen from the ALK-positive NSCLC study of once-daily oral DV-301. As written, it cannot be implemented under the stated objectives and eligibility criteria; it also bypasses combination-dose evaluation.
findings.guidance_quote: When a drug is intended for use in combination with another drug, the dosage of the combination regimen should be optimized.

findings.span: Pharmacokinetic blood samples will be collected only before dosing and at 1 hour after the first administration; no samples will be obtained after repeat dosing or during the expected accumulation period.
findings.claim: This contradicts the intensive Day 1/Day 15 and repeated trough-sampling plan. If followed, it would not characterize the stated autoinduction, accumulation or steady-state exposure needed for dose selection.
findings.guidance_quote: Pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic data should be collected to characterize exposure–response relationships for efficacy and safety.

findings.span: Concomitant medications will be recorded at enrollment, but no interaction studies or dedicated pharmacokinetic analyses will be conducted before selecting the recommended Phase 3 dose.
findings.claim: Enrollment-only medication recording misses changes during treatment, while the categorical absence of interaction or dedicated PK evaluation leaves drug-interaction effects on exposure unresolved before Phase 3 dose selection.
findings.guidance_quote: Information on the effects of demographic factors, concomitant disease, and concomitant drugs on the dose-response relationship should also be obtained.

findings.span: ECGs will be performed at baseline and periodically for PR interval prolongation.
findings.claim: “Periodically” gives no timed ECG schedule or trigger-based assessment for early or worsening PR prolongation and AV block, despite specifying AV-block dose-modification rules.
findings.guidance_quote: The rights, safety, and well-being of trial participants are the most important considerations and should prevail over interests of science and society.

findings.span: Primary (Phase 2): Objective response rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1, including intracranial response, at the selected recommended Phase 2 dose (RP2D).
findings.claim: The endpoint does not distinguish overall ORR from intracranial response or specify the intracranial analysis population, including whether baseline measurable brain lesions are required. This leaves a stated primary efficacy assessment insufficiently defined.
findings.guidance_quote: Critical to quality factors are attributes of a trial that are fundamental to the protection of participants, the reliability and interpretability of the trial results, and the decisions made based on the trial results.

findings.span: Intensive PK sampling on Cycle 1 Day 1 and Day 15 (pre-dose, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 24 h post-dose) in all escalation subjects to characterize autoinduction; steady-state trough sampling every cycle in the randomized cohorts.
findings.claim: Nine scheduled samples on each of two days for every escalation participant impose substantial sampling and visit burden. The protocol does not justify why all participants, rather than a fit-for-purpose subset, need this schedule.
findings.guidance_quote: The trial should be designed to be operationally feasible and avoid unnecessary complexity, procedures and data collection.

findings.span: Tumor assessments, including brain MRI, every 6 weeks.
findings.claim: The unqualified schedule appears to require repeated brain MRI even for participants without baseline CNS disease. Its necessity for all participants is not established despite the time and procedural burden.
findings.guidance_quote: The trial should be designed to be operationally feasible and avoid unnecessary complexity, procedures and data collection.
